title: Morningstar Analytics - Private Routing and Regional Constraints Discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Morningstar's network posture and constraints for a private Redwood deployment. Key topics: VPC peering options, PrivateLink vs. VPC endpoints, egress IP requirements for financial regulators, region gating for EU-only data, and pilot scope + timeline. Customer leaning toward Private deployment in their AWS VPC with strict egress whitelisting and SOC2 compliance needs.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Egress IP staticness and NAT/firewall allowances
Private control plane vs customer-managed control plane
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we have samira and eli from our se team.
[00:06] Tom: hey thanks, we appreciate it. joining from Morningstar — Tom here, VP of Eng, and i've got alex and priya on the line.
[00:12] Jordan: awesome. quick agenda: understand your networking constraints, security needs, timeline for pilot, and then map out next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Priya: yep that works. important for us: all inference traffic must terminate inside our AWS for EU customers and we need a reproducible egress ip set for our firewalls.
[00:30] Samira: got it. just to confirm, do you have a preferred pattern? private endpoints, privatelink, or peering?
[00:36] Alex: we prefer something that doesn't force us to open a bunch of cross-account rules. our infra team likes PrivateLink because it's single-vpc endpoint and more controlled.
[00:44] Eli: just a note — PrivateLink is supported but there are limits around cross-region. if you need EU-only, we can provision endpoints in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1, but cross-region calls will route differently.
[00:58] Tom: EU-only is a must. our product teams are feeding eu customers and legal won't allow data to leave region. can redwood host the model and control plane in eu only?
[01:10] Jordan: yes — we offer private deployment with control plane options. for strict data residency, we can do a private control plane in your VPC or deploy our private package into your account. the difference is whether you want us to operate the control plane or you operate it.
[01:26] Priya: we prefer customer-managed control plane so audit logs and keys remain in our KMS. can we bring our own KMS (BYOK)?
[01:33] Samira: absolutely — we support BYOK via AWS KMS and HSM integrations. we just need key policies and IAM roles in the onboarding docs.
[01:40] Devin: for egress ips — our firewall team needs 3 static /29s to allow across the perimeter. any way redwood can provide static egress ips from the deployment?
[01:50] Eli: static egress ip is tricky with autoscaling. typical pattern: we can put a NAT bastion or use egress through a fixed NAT gateway in your account so the egress IPs are owned by you and remain static. that is our recommended pattern for private deployments in the customer VPC.
[02:06] Alex: so to be clear you recommend we own the NAT gateway to guarantee ip stability?
[02:11] Eli: yes — if you host the dataplane in your VPC or host a peered VPC with a stable NAT, you control the egress ip space. if we host the dataplane in a Redwood-managed VPC, we can allocate static egress but it's less common for customers with strict whitelisting.
[02:26] Tom: what about transit gateway? we already have a TGW in our infra, would peering into that simplify things?
[02:33] Samira: we can attach to a TGW — the typical model is cross-account VPC attachment to your TGW. that's scalable for multi-region. only caveat is routing complexity and we'd need to make sure there's no hairpinning or asymmetric routing.
[02:47] Priya: asym routing is a red flag for us. we need symmetric paths for packet inspection.
[02:52] Eli: we usually request a short routing diagram from your network team. we can validate with a design review to ensure symmetric paths and talk about route tables.
[02:59] Jordan: timeline question — if we start a pilot, how fast can Morningstar onboard in terms of networking changes?
[03:06] Alex: we can open security exceptions within 1-2 weeks for a test VPC, but production firewall rules and egress whitelists will take 4-6 weeks.
[03:14] Tom: our priority is to validate latency and throughput for our realtime inference use cases. can redwood provide benchmark instances or a perf run?
[03:21] Samira: yep we can run a small perf benchmark — typically we spin up a mirrored environment in your eu region and run a 2-3 day token throughput test using representative prompts. we'll need sample prompts and expected p95 latency targets.
[03:35] Tom: p95 target is <200ms for short prompts (<256 tokens) for the customer-facing APIs.
[03:43] Samira: okay noted. one more question: do you have any vendor restrictions, like no third-party cloud peering or embargoed providers?
[03:50] Priya: legal flagged Anthropic in an old policy note, but that's about model sourcing not network. we do have a rule about outbound endpoints — no connections to CN regions (china) from EU workloads.
[04:02] Jordan: understood — region gating is doable. we can restrict model artifacts and inference compute to selected regions.
[04:09] Devin: what's the split between private endpoints and peering from an ops perspective? which is easier to maintain?
[04:15] Eli: ops-wise, PrivateLink is simpler for cross-account service access with fewer route-table changes. Peering/TGW is more flexible for large traffic volumes and multi-subnet control. but PrivateLink has fewer maintenance windows and less routing complexity.
[04:30] Alex: any cost delta? TGW attachments and data egress inside aws vs PrivateLink?
[04:36] Samira: PrivateLink can be slightly cheaper for low throughput but TGW scales better. there are per-GB egress and per-connection costs for both — we'll share a cost primer.
[04:46] Tom: security — can we get audit logs and traces shipped to our SIEM?
[04:51] Jordan: yes. for private deployments we can forward audit logs to your S3 + CloudWatch or push to an event stream (Kinesis / Kafka). since you're customer-managed, logs stay in your account.
[05:02] Priya: and SSO? we need SAML + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC for token scopes.
[05:07] Samira: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. for API keys and token scopes, we have RBAC at the org and team level — we can map to your IdP groups.
[05:18] Alex: any dependencies on specific CNI or DNS setups? we use a private hosted zone and some customers have split-horizon DNS.
[05:25] Eli: that's common — we can register private endpoints in your private hosted zone or we can create an override. we'll need access to the zone delegation details for setup.
[05:34] Jordan: quick nit — latency check: if we peer within eu-west-1 that should meet your <200ms p95 generally?
[05:42] Samira: yes should be fine, but depends on model size and batching. our runtime has optimized kernels and batching config that we tune during pilot.
[05:52] Tom: about model versions — do you allow us to pin a model and disable automatic updates? we need reproducibility for regulatory audits.
[06:00] Samira: yes. you can pin model versions and we support controlled rollouts. automatic updates are opt-in and we can do canary and A/B tests under your control.
[06:09] Priya: also retention — how long do logs live by default?
[06:13] Jordan: default retention is 90 days in hosted but for private deployments retention is configurable and since logs are in your account you decide retention.
[06:21] Alex: okay good. can you sketch a minimal pilot: what steps do we need network-wise, and who's responsible?
[06:28] Eli: pilot MVP: 1) create a test VPC (or allow us to peer into an existing test VPC), 2) provision one private endpoint or TGW attachment in eu region, 3) provide a NAT gateway for static egress ips, 4) share sample prompts and expected SLAs, 5) run perf tests for 48-72 hours. responsibility: network attachments and NAT are customer-owned; we handle deployment and perf harness.
[06:49] Devin: that seems reasonable. for step 3 we can carve two /29s and allocate them to the NAT.
[06:55] Samira: perfect. one more item: encryption in transit — do you require mTLS?
[07:00] Priya: mTLS would be preferred for control plane; for dataplane we need TLS1.2+ and cert pinning if possible.
[07:08] Eli: we support mTLS for control plane connections and TLS for dataplane. cert pinning can be discussed in the onboarding doc.
[07:16] Jordan: alright before we go into Q&A — can i summarize next steps?
[07:20] Tom: please do.
[07:22] Jordan: action items: 1) we'll send the private deployment playbook and network checklist, 2) samira will scope the perf plan and required sample prompts, 3) morningstar to confirm egress ip allocation and share NAT plan and routing diagram, 4) schedule a design review with your network team next week.
[07:39] Priya: add: we'll need an excerpt of your SOC2 scope and your KMS integration doc.
[07:45] Jordan: noted, we'll include security docs and SOC2 summary.
[07:49] Alex: and pricing ballpark for dedicated private nodes? we need an order of magnitude for budgeting.
[07:55] Jordan: we'll send a starter pricing sheet for pilot and a committed Dedicated estimate.
[08:00] Tom: cool. any blockers from our side?
[08:03] Devin: none immediate. we'll start on the NAT and get the routing diagram by monday.
[08:09] Samira: great. quick FAQ: if you later want to move to a Redwood-managed VPC we can talk about egress ip SLAs but we'd prefer customer-owned NAT for strict whitelisting.
[08:20] Priya: understood. thanks all.
[08:23] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.
[08:26] -- end of recording --
